cpu_farm_interruption: the T001 CPU farm was interrupted by a host crash while C.D07, C.D09-C.D12 and C.all were ~40 min into their runs (C.D01-C.D06 had already hit the 160-min cap at ~1500/4000 steps). They are not re-run on the CPU: they are absent from the CPU farm state, which the frozen table counts as failed. Only the planned A and B D05 determinism refits are completed on the CPU
device_control: B is refitted on ROCm on every fold: B(ROCm) vs B(CPU) measures the device effect; B(ROCm) vs C(ROCm) is the device-matched architecture contrast
disclosure: frozen after the CPU A and B results were visible (A Genesis mean ER 0.105, B 0.155); no C score existed. The amendment changes no threshold and no model setting
reporting: the unchanged T001 table and rule are evaluated on two views: 'rocm_bc' (A CPU, B ROCm, C ROCm) and 'mixed' (A CPU, B CPU, C ROCm). Both are reported as AMENDMENT results next to the pre-registered class (C failed under the CPU caps), never replacing it. A C that qualifies only under the amendment is reported as such; SEG-076-T002 admission follows the pre-registered class

resources.caps_basis: uncontended single-process ROCm probe: B 0.038 s/step (~2.5 min per 4000 steps), C 0.54 s/step (~36 min); caps ~3x those plus inference
resources.why_serial: two host (WSL2) crashes occurred while 3 ROCm probe processes plus a CPU self-test were started on top of 6 running CPU fits (~11.5 GB RSS on a 16 GB host); the amendment therefore runs ONE ROCm process at a time and nothing heavier than one 2-thread CPU determinism refit beside it

selftest: fit_bc_device / infer_bc_device on the CPU are bitwise identical to the frozen fit_bc / infer_bc (6 steps on the D05-fold training set, B and C: parameters and inference)
trigger: every planned C fit exceeded the frozen 160-min CPU cap (C ~5.5 s/step under the 6-fit CPU farm vs 0.8 s/step in the probe); C is 'failed' under the frozen plan and that pre-registered T001 class is unchanged
unchanged: network (segarecomp_xplat_models.build_bc), M4 recipe, 4000 steps, seed 1, folds, data, metrics, expansion rule; fit_bc_device is a line-for-line copy of the frozen fit_bc with tensors moved to the device, proven bitwise identical to fit_bc on CPU by `selftest`
